stewart_read: The intro is stumbled and incomplete — the rep never re-establishes clear legitimacy (no state mention, no clear restatement of the form context) after the customer's suspicious opener, leaving 'is this legit' unresolved.
coaching_implication: Coach a clean recovery line for when a customer challenges the call's purpose immediately — restate company name, reference to the specific form, and a low-pressure next step, spoken fluently rather than trailing off.

quote: I I just simply want information on the services you provide and the cost of for for those services.
stewart_read: This is a textbook price_estimate_before_design trigger with a canonical redirect available ('cost depends on roof, shading, usage — if you've got 30 seconds I can get you an actual design with real numbers'). The rep never deploys anything close to this redirect.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may be avoiding sounding scripted by not using canned rebuttal language. Rejected — the rep offers no redirect at all, scripted or improvised, at 01:02 or after.
coaching_implication: Drill the price_estimate_before_design rebuttal until it's reflexive; this exact customer phrasing is common and the schema already has the answer.

quote: I mean, I I myself don't have, like, any price details.
stewart_read: This is an honest admission rather than a fabrication, which is the better of the three knowledge-gap failure modes, but it's offered with no recovery — no redirect to the specialist, no reframing of why the setter doesn't carry pricing.
coaching_implication: Pair transparency with a bridge: 'I don't carry pricing because it's fully custom to your home — that's exactly what our design specialist builds for you on the call' turns the same honesty into forward motion.

quote: I totally get you. Yes. I mean, here at Allynos, we don't really just send quotes out of the mail or anything like that,
stewart_read: The rep does invoke the correct hard-rule policy (no mailed proposals) but delivers it thinly, without the schema's reasoning ('proposals require full explanation, otherwise confusing') and misstates the company name as 'Allynos,' which undercuts the legitimacy the intro already failed to lock in.
coaching_implication: Flag the company-name slip for review — even a single misstatement compounds skepticism with an already-suspicious customer. Drill the full canonical line, not a fragment of it.

stewart_read: By the customer's second restatement, the rep has an opening to offer the small-ask move ('can I have 30 seconds to explain why a phone conversation gets you better numbers than a mailed quote') but does not attempt it.
coaching_implication: Coach the small-ask pattern here — it exists in the schema for exactly this kind of stated resistance and was never tried.

quote: Okay. Well, yeah. I mean, we're we're not able to do that here, so I'll just take you off my list.
stewart_read: The call terminates with a unilateral rep decision to drop the lead — no DQ rule was met, no supervisor consult, no attempt at a smaller next step (e.g., a specialist call solely to discuss numbers). This is the rep exiting the call, not the customer.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have judged the lead unworkable and cut losses efficiently. Rejected — the customer never said no; he said 'if you're willing to do that, fine... if not, no problem,' leaving the door open for a different offer the rep never tried.
coaching_implication: This is the single most correctable moment on the call — review with the rep what a bridge offer sounds like before defaulting to removal.
